Mani stones carved with Om Mani Padme Hum by master craftsman Yanchong Lodil
festivals: Bumchu (holy water) ceremony - the monastery's main annual festival, held on the 14th and 15th day of the first Tibetan lunar month (February-March); the water level in the sacred vase is read to predict Sikkim's fortunes for the coming year

history.dynasty: Namgyal dynasty (Sikkimese monarchy); extended and renovated during the reign of the third Chogyal Chakdor Namgyal
history.period: Late 17th/early 18th century - FOUNDING DATE CONFLICT (verify): Wikipedia gives founded 1641 by Ngadak Sempa Chempo (one of the three lamas who crowned the first Chogyal at Yuksom) and extended/renovated in 1717 during the third Chogyal Chakdor Namgyal; several travel sources say the monastery was built in 1717
history.summary: CSV TOWN NOTE: the CSV town 'Geyzing' is approximate - Tashiding is a town/area of its own about 19-27 km from Yuksom and about 27-40 km by road from Gyalshing (Geyzing), in Gyalshing district; town corrected to Tashiding. Described as the most sacred and holiest monastery of Sikkim, called the 'Heart of Sikkim/Denzong' for its religious sacredness. It belongs to the Nyingma order. The monastery sits atop a heart-shaped hill between the Rathong and Rangit rivers, with views of Kanchenjunga; tradition holds Guru Padmasambhava blessed the site in the 8th century. Its treasures include the Thong-Wa-Rang-Dol chorten (built by Lhatsun Chempo; a mere sight of it is said to wash away sins) and the sacred Bumchu vase of holy water, consecrated by Padmasambhava in 8th-century Tibet and rediscovered in the 17th century. Four sacred meditation caves surround the town in the cardinal directions (Sharchog Bephug east, Khandozangphu south, Dechenpug west, Lhari Nyingphug north). It is part of the Buddhist pilgrimage circuit of Dubdi, Norbugang, Pemayangtse, Rabdentse, Sanga Choeling and Khecheopalri Lake. Religious affiliation verified as Nyingma Tibetan Buddhism - NOT a Hindu temple.

name: Tashiding Monastery
town_description: Tashiding, in Gyalshing district, is the nearest town to Tashiding Monastery, set on a hilltop between the Rathong and Rangit rivers at about 1,465 m. Four sacred meditation caves surround it in the cardinal directions. It lies about 19-23 km from Yuksom and about 27-40 km by road from Gyalshing (Geyzing) via Legship (verify).

travel.airport: Nearest airport is Bagdogra (IXB), approx. 140-160 km (verify); Pakyong Airport is closer but has limited flights.
travel.railway: Nearest major railway station is New Jalpaiguri (NJP), approx. 140-160 km (verify).
travel.road: About 40 km by road from Gyalshing/Pelling via Legship (verify); bus service reported from Gyalshing to Tashiding; a trekkers' hut is available at Tashiding.

visitor_information.best_time: March to June for pleasant weather; February-March for the Bumchu festival (dates follow the Tibetan lunar calendar).
visitor_information.opening_hours: One source reports 7 AM-6 PM (verify). The monastery is reached by a steep uphill walk from the road.
